subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Brooklyn Bridge
description: A quick, practical guide to The Brooklyn Bridge.

hook.text: In 1883, the Brooklyn Bridge was the longest suspension bridge ever built — by far.

buildup.text: John Roebling designed it, but died before construction began. His son took over.

discovery.text: Workers in caissons 78 feet underwater suffered decompression sickness — the bends.

twist.text: Washington Roebling became paralyzed from the bends and directed work by telescope.

climax.text: It took 14 years. On opening day, 150,000 people walked across in celebration.

punchline.text: A bridge built by a family who sacrificed everything for it.

quiz.question: What debilitating condition affected Brooklyn Bridge workers?
options: Lead poisoning from the paint used on the cables
Decompression sickness from working in pressurized caissons underwater
Heat stroke from working in direct sunlight on the towers
